medications.duration: Lifelong — review every 6 months and titrate to target <140/90 mmHg; increase to 10 mg if needed
medications.purpose: First‑line antihypertensive for Afro‑Caribbean adult; control stage‑2 hypertension in pregnancy
medications.nice_justification: NG136 recommends a CCB (amlodipine preferred) as step 1 therapy for patients aged ≥55 or of Afro‑Caribbean origin

medications.duration: Until delivery — stop 24 h before planned birth
medications.purpose: Prophylaxis of pre‑eclampsia in high‑risk pregnant woman (chronic hypertension, Black ethnicity, pre‑diabetes)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG133 recommends low‑dose aspirin 75 mg daily for women at high risk of pre‑eclampsia

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine modestly inhibits CYP3A4, which may increase tramadol plasma levels by ~10‑20 %
interactions_checked.action: Monitor for increased sedation or constipation; adjust tramadol dose if clinically significant

interactions_checked.interaction: CYP3A4 inhibition may raise oxycodone concentrations modestly
interactions_checked.action: Observe for enhanced opioid effects; consider dose reduction if excessive sedation occurs

interactions_checked.interaction: Minimal interaction; theoretical slight increase in fentanyl levels
interactions_checked.action: No dose change required; monitor for respiratory depression

contraindications.reason: Teratogenic; contraindicated in pregnancy (NG136 contraindicates ACE‑I in pregnancy)
contraindications.alternative: Calcium channel blocker (amlodipine) or pregnancy‑specific agents (labetalol, methyldopa)

contraindications.reason: Teratogenic and contraindicated in pregnancy; also dual RAAS blockade with ACE‑I is prohibited
No added benefit and increased renal risk; both are contraindicated in pregnancy
Increase blood pressure and risk renal impairment in pregnancy

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m²; renal function will be checked before any future ACE‑I/ARB or diuretic initiation.
Gestational age not specified – choice of amlodipine assumes second trimester or later; obstetric team to confirm safety if <20 weeks.
QRISK score not calculated – required by NG136 for cardiovascular risk assessment; will be performed at next antenatal visit.
Liver function tests not available – needed before initiating statin therapy postpartum.
Allergy status unknown – will verify before starting any new medication.
treatment_summary: Start amlodipine 5 mg daily as first‑line antihypertensive per NG136 for Afro‑Caribbean pregnancy, with dose titration to achieve BP <140/90 mmHg. Add low‑dose aspirin 75 mg nightly for pre‑eclampsia prophylaxis per NG133. Monitor for modest CYP3A4 interactions with existing opioid regimen and review renal function, gestational age, and QRISK before any future therapy.
